target.title: fix(agents): drop orphaned thinking blocks when NO_REPLY text leaves an assistant message with only thinking content (#99620)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

NO_REPLY yield-turn assistant messages with thinking blocks cause a permanent 400 loop after gateway restart. Dropping the NO_REPLY text without the companion thinking block leaves orphaned thinking blocks that merge with adjacent assistant messages into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`, which Anthropic rejects as "cannot be modified."

- **Observed impact**: 5 production sessions bricked in a single day (2026-07-03) per issue reporter. Each session requires a manual `/new` to recover.
- **Root cause chain**: `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` drops NO_REPLY text but preserves thinking → yield artifacts cleaned up → adjacent assistant merge → `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]` → HTTP 400
- **Existing guards miss this**: `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures` and compaction-only strippers do not fire because the signatures are cryptographically valid — they are simply stale from a prior provider context.
- **Fix location**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` in `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Issue: #99620
- Related (broader completed-turn thinking replay policy): #99383
- Related (same symptom, different trigger): #98760

## Evidence

### Payload comparison

Running `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` (the actual OpenClaw code path used in production) demonstrates the fix:

```console
Input (5 messages):
  [0] user        "hi"
  [1] assistant   [thinking(sig_yield) + text("NO_REPLY")]   ← yield-turn
  [2] assistant   [thinking(sig_next) + tool_use]             ← tool-turn
  [3] user        "[tool result]"
  [4] assistant   [text("Done.")]

=== Without fix ===
After normalizeAssistantReplayContent:
  [1] assistant  [thinking]              ← orphaned! NO_REPLY dropped, thinking survives
  [2] assistant  [thinking, toolCall]

Adjacent assistant merge → assistant[thinking(sig_yield), thinking(sig_next), tool_use]
                                       ↑━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━↑
→ 2 thinking blocks in one message → Anthropic rejects with 400 "cannot be modified"

=== With fix (PR #99772) ===
After normalizeAssistantReplayContent:
  [1] assistant  [thinking, toolCall]    ← yield-turn dropped (fix fires)
  [2] user       "[tool result]"
  [3] assistant  [text("Done.")]

No adjacent merge → assistant[thinking(sig_next), tool_use]
→ 1 thinking block per message → Anthropic accepts with 200
```

### How the fix works

The change adds 4 lines of logic to `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`:

```typescript
// 1. Track whether any silent-reply text was dropped
let hasSilentText = false;

// 2. In both text-drop paths (direct NO_REPLY match AND
//    metadata-stripped-to-NO_REPLY), set hasSilentText = true

// 3. After the loop, if silent text was dropped AND remaining
//    content is only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks:
if (hasSilentText && sanitizedContent.every(isThinkingOrRedacted)) {
  return null;  // drop the entire message
}
```

Three scenarios are covered:

| Text block shape | hasSilentText set? | Guard fires? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"NO_REPLY"` (direct match) | Yes | Yes | Message dropped ✓ |
| `"metadata...\n\nNO_REPLY"` (metadata stripped) | Yes (fix! See P2 below) | Yes | Message dropped ✓ |
| `"NO_REPLY"` + `tool_use` sibling | Yes | No (tool_use exists) | Message preserved ✓ |

### Metadata-stripped path (P2 finding, now fixed)

When `stripInternalMetadataForDisplay` removes conversation metadata and reveals NO_REPLY text, `hasSilentText` must also be set. The initial PR missed this path; it was identified by ClawSweeper review and fixed with a regression test:

```console
Input:  [user, assistant(thinking + "metadata block with NO_REPLY tail")]
Output: [user]  ← yield-turn dropped ✓
```

### Test results (all passing)

| Suite | Tests | Status |
|---|---|---|
| replay-history.test.ts | 33 (4 new + 29 existing) | All pass |
| thinking.test.ts | 48 | All pass |
| sanitize-session-history.test.ts | 76 | All pass |
| **Total** | **157** | **All pass** |

### Verification scripts

Two scripts are included in the repo:

| Script | Purpose | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/demo-no-reply-fix.ts` | Source-level payload comparison using OpenClaw's actual normalization pipeline | Nothing (runs with `tsx`) |
| `scripts/live-test-no-reply-thinking.mjs` | Live Anthropic API round-trip showing before-fix rejection and after-fix acceptance | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with thinking-enabled model access |

**Live round-trip not yet performed**: I do not have a thinking-enabled Anthropic API key. The script is ready for any maintainer to run with their own credentials. A compatible DeepSeek proxy was tested locally, but it does not enforce Anthropic's signed-thinking replay validation, so the actual 400 → 200 transition could not be reproduced there.

## Root Cause

`normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` (line 225 of `replay-history.ts`) drops silent-reply text blocks but preserves companion thinking blocks. When the replay-history pipeline subsequently removes the yield artifacts that separated the yield-turn from the next assistant message, two assistants become adjacent. The provider-agnostic `validateAnthropicTurns` merges them, producing a single assistant content array with two signed thinking blocks — a shape that Anthropic rejects.

Provenance:
- `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`: carried forward from the Jun 25 runtime refactor (`af906225fa`)
- `validateAnthropicTurns`: carried forward from the same refactor, adjacent-assistant merge behavior introduced in `462c076a24e2`
- Made visible by: users running NO_REPLY yield patterns with thinking-enabled models
- Confidence: **clear** (deterministic source-level reproduction)

## Regression Test Plan

- `replay-history.test.ts` — 4 new tests:
  1. `"drops orphaned thinking blocks from a stop-turn whose only text was NO_REPLY"`
  2. `"drops orphaned thinking blocks before a follow-up tool-use assistant to prevent adjacent merge"`
  3. `"preserves thinking blocks when a NO_REPLY assistant has a tool_use sibling"`
  4. `"drops orphaned thinking when metadata strip reveals NO_REPLY"`
- `thinking.test.ts` — 48 tests pass unchanged
- `sanitize-session-history.test.ts` — 76 tests pass unchanged

## User-visible Behavior Changes

Sessions affected by NO_REPLY yield-turn thinking merge will recover on the next provider request (orphaned thinking blocks stripped) instead of entering a permanent 400 loop. Users with no NO_REPLY yield-turns experience no behavioral change.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **tool_use companion present**: Guarded by `every()` — only orphaned thinking (no tool_use, no text) triggers the drop.
- **Legitimate thinking-only assistant**: The issue reporter confirms such messages carry no replay value (stale signatures from a prior provider context). PR #99383 takes the broader approach of dropping all completed-turn thinking blocks.
- **Metadata-stripped silent text**: Both the direct and metadata-stripped paths now set `hasSilentText`, ensuring the guard fires consistently.
- **Compatibility**: No config, env, or migration impact. Zero-token stop turns and normal replay paths are unaffected.

## Relationship to PR #99383

This PR is a narrow fix for the NO_REPLY yield-turn merge path specifically. PR #99383 (Sunjae-k) takes the broader approach of dropping all completed-turn thinking blocks. The two are complementary:

- If #99383 lands first → this PR's guard becomes a safety net for the NO_REPLY path
- If this PR lands first → the NO_REPLY yield-turn class is closed while #99383 covers remaining completion-replay surface
- Either way → both addresses the same structural gap at different granularity levels

## Maintainer options

As outlined in the ClawSweeper review:

1. **Accept this narrow fix** — the payload-structure evidence and 157 tests demonstrate correctness; live Anthropic proof script is ready for verification
2. **Fold into #99383** — carry the test cases into the broader replay branch
3. **Require live Anthropic proof** — run `scripts/live-test-no-reply-thinking.mjs` with API credentials

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: NO_REPLY yield with thinking, full adjacency chain, tool_use boundary, metadata-stripped NO_REPLY
- What you did NOT verify: Live Anthropic API round-trip (no API key available to contributor)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No
